scores.0-4: Incomplete or fundamentally flawed understanding; cannot explain key definitions or operations.
scores.5-7: Understands the core concept; communicates basic syntax or principles but misses trade-offs, internal mechanics, or edge cases.
scores.8-10: Mastery demonstrated; explains internal implementation, architectural trade-offs, performance implications, and practical examples.

scores.0-4: Syntax errors, incorrect algorithmic approach, or fails standard sample cases.
scores.5-7: Functional brute-force or sub-optimal approach; passes primary test cases but misses edge cases or suboptimal time/space complexity.
scores.8-10: Optimal algorithmic complexity (e.g. O(n) instead of O(n^2)), handles null/empty/boundary inputs, clean idiomatic variable naming.

star_criteria.Situation: Set the context, company, or technical challenge clearly.
star_criteria.Task: Defined personal responsibility and role in the problem.
star_criteria.Action: Detailed specific engineering decisions or personal initiatives taken.
star_criteria.Result: Quantified business impact, performance gain, or lessons learned.
